answers.rationale: Kara repeatedly prefers a standard included window when there is no schedule or connection pressure, and declines fees merely to sit farther forward. With no post-arrival constraint, 28A is the best fit; 9C gives up the window and the paid options add unnecessary cost.

When a window cannot be selected normally, Kara uses a free window request and a check-in reminder rather than paying a premium or worsening an otherwise better itinerary solely for immediate seat visibility.

For partner travel, Kara explicitly prioritizes adjacent seats over obtaining a window, and repeatedly keeps free adjacent pairs rather than paying to improve seat position. The free 22B/22C pair best preserves that priority.

With no connection, bag, or immediate-arrival obligation, Kara's default is an included window. She also avoids needless discomfort trade-offs, so the rear-galley window is inferior; 21A keeps the window preference without that drawback.
